title: Defense in the Reverse Fragment: RL-Based Partial Netlist Hardware Trojan Detection
problem: Hardware Trojan detection methods assume complete netlists, but practical reverse engineering yields incomplete/partial information, reducing detection accuracy and stability.
motivation: Enable practical hardware Trojan detection from partial netlist information obtained through reverse engineering of real circuits.
method: RE-PNRL: Reinforcement Learning-based framework for reconstructing partial netlists using node-level transition probabilities. Clustering-based hardware Trojan detection using complete netlist reconstruction.
key_novelty: First hardware Trojan detection framework addressing practical partial-netlist scenarios from reverse engineering.
contributions: 66.39% TPR and 73.72% TNR on partial-netlist HT detection
96.80% TPR and 94.80% TNR on clustering-based complete-netlist detection
RL-based netlist reconstruction from partial information
Effective across different levels of netlist missingness
limitations: Evaluated on Trojan benchmarks; specific to netlist-based detection methodology.
primary_theme: RL-based hardware trojan detection with partial netlist information
